text:
emily (People Ops): Quick Q — we have an on-site interview next Thu. Candidate booked flight themselves and asked for reimbursement. Also the hiring team wants to take the candidate to dinner; one interviewer might bring a +1. How do we handle reimbursements, guest meals, and receipts? @sahil can you advise?

sahil (Recruiting Ops): Short answer: reimburse candidate travel actuals (economy cap), but candidate does not get per-diem. Need proof of travel (boarding pass/e-ticket) + proof of payment. For interviewer-hosted dinners: company can cover candidate portion but guest/partner is non-reimbursable. Pre-approve any interviewer expenses > $200.

Aaron (Finance): Confirming — candidate travel = actuals up to cap. For dinners, preferred flow is to put meal on company card. If interviewer pays personally, submit expense but annotate which lines are candidate-related. We will not reimburse guest/partner items. Receipts required: itemized restaurant receipt or card statement + attendee note.

Lina (Hiring Manager): How should we annotate or split a receipt if the interviewer paid and guest included?

sahil (Recruiting Ops): In the expense app add a comment: "Candidate dinner - Jane D - candidate portion $XX" and upload the full receipt. If the app supports line-item split, use that. If not, attach a quick spreadsheet or a photo with the portion circled and a short note. Finance will audit if unclear.

emily (People Ops): If candidate stayed in an Airbnb or used a private arrangement, what do we need?

Aaron (Finance): For non-hotel lodging we need host receipts showing guest name/dates + proof of payment (card or checkout email). No cash-only Airbnb claims without a host invoice. We prefer corporate/OTA bookings for consistency but will reimburse valid receipts.

travel-bot: TravelPolicyBot: Reminder — candidate travel reimbursements: must be submitted within 30 days of travel; uploads required: boarding pass/e-ticket, proof of payment, itemized lodging receipt (if applicable). Any single reimbursement > $2,000 requires travel@redwood approval.

Jeff (Hiring Manager): One variant — candidate arrived with partner and partner's meal $42 was on the same card. We only want to reimburse candidate portion. Do we need the interviewer to void/issue separate receipt?

Aaron (Finance): No need to void. Upload the full receipt, indicate partner portion as non-reimbursable in the note, and show your math for the split. If unclear, finance will ask for a photo or statement showing who was present.

emily (People Ops): If candidate asks for cash advance before travel (they're external), we don't do per-diem/advance for candidates — reimburse after submission only.

sahil (Recruiting Ops): Also — for travel arranged by recruiting (we book), we cover travel + candidate meals. For team-hosted social events that include non-candidates (partners), those partner costs are not covered.

emily (People Ops): Quick copy-paste template for the expense form to speed things up:```
Expense title: Candidate travel reimbursement - Jane Doe
Total amount: $XXX.XX
Items:
- Flight (e-ticket attached) $YYY.YY
- Lodging (itemized receipt attached) $ZZ.ZZ
- Dinner - candidate portion (itemized receipt attached) $AA.AA
Notes: Candidate travel approved by recruiting@redwood on 2026-03-17. Partner/guest portion excluded from reimbursement.```:thumbsup:

Lina (Hiring Manager): Perfect — I'll tell the interviewer to either use the company card or submit with a clear split. Thanks everyone.

emily (People Ops): I'll add this to the recruiting playbook and put a one-pager in the interview packet. If anyone sees a corner case (e.g., visa courier fees tied to candidate travel) flag it here and we'll confirm next steps.
